name: Pakistani nationalism
summary: Pakistani nationalism treats Pakistan as the homeland of the subcontinent's Muslims, a nation defined by Islam and an Indo-Muslim civilisation under the Two-Nation Theory. It is state nationalism that also draws on Islam, gives the army a guardian role over the state and its ideology, and prides itself on the nuclear deterrent and a firm claim to Kashmir. It combines a democratic and minority-protecting founding rhetoric (Jinnah, the Objectives Resolution) with an Islamic constitutional framework.
scope: The mainstream state nationalism of Pakistan as drawn from Iqbal's Allahabad Address, the Lahore Resolution, Jinnah's speeches including 11 August 1947, the 1949 Objectives Resolution and the Ayub and Zia era Islamisation and education policy. It excludes ethnic and regional nationalisms (Baloch, Pashtun, Sindhi, Bengali) and revisionist pre-Islamic strands, and does not represent the Islamist parties' theocratic programme beyond where it is mainstream.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a central nationalist theme; the state-building tradition and Jinnah's welfare-of-the-people language suggest mild support, inferred rather than documented.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from Jinnah's stress on the welfare of the common people; sources never discuss wage policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents are split: Muslim League tradition is pro-business while the PPP strand and state-led development favour intervention.

public-ownership.rationale: Pakistan's nationalists have both nationalised (1970s PPP) and privatised; the ideology itself is indifferent.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Jinnah's attacks on profiteering and the poor's welfare; no source gives a tax position.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalism as such takes no line on organised labour; military and League traditions have been wary of unions while the PPP strand backs them.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Objectives Resolution subjects rights to law and public morality, but nationalists are split on how absolute property is.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Jinnah condemned black-marketing and profiteering, from which mild support for regulation is inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: Jinnah's speech stresses uplift of the poor and the Objectives Resolution invokes social justice, so welfare cuts are unlikely to be endorsed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is not part of this nationalism; the Objectives Resolution speaks of social justice without endorsing it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A militarised security-state nationalism treats counter-terror and security services as guardians of the nation, so surveillance is broadly accepted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Islamisation measures and the Islamic-republic framing make drug legalisation alien to the mainstream; the state prohibits intoxicants.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents back blasphemy-style limits on speech against religion, yet not hate speech laws as such; the mainstream is split.

strong-leader.rationale: The army-led strand favours strong rule while the League tradition claims democracy; adherents are genuinely split.

state-harmful.rationale: Pakistani nationalism is state nationalism built around creating and defending a state, so abolishing it is unthinkable.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed by the sources; the state-arms stress favours control but gun culture is widespread among adherents.

empower-police-military.rationale: The army calls itself guardian of the nation and ideology and holds very high public trust, so more funding and authority is consistent with its core. No cited source states this directly; it follows from the documented principles.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Islamisation under Zia criminalised zina and the Islamic-republic framing opposes legal sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: A unitary-minded state nationalism distrusts regionalism and treats ethnic nationalist parties as marginal and divisive, favouring national authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Hudood punishments exist but Jinnah's civil-rule tradition is not explicit on prisons; adherents are split.

traditional-family.rationale: Pakistani nationalism rests on Islamic identity with conservative family norms, reflected in Islamisation measures.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Islamic-republic nationalism treats this as contrary to Islam and law, and it is not legal in Pakistan.

abortion-legal.rationale: Mainstream Islamic-conservative position treats abortion as impermissible in most cases; the Islamisation of law reflects this.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and Article 2A put Islam in public life; however Jinnah's secular-sounding speech keeps some adherents ambivalent.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an issue for this ideology; minority protections are promised but racial redress is not a theme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Conservative Islamic framing of gender roles in Pakistani nationalism rejects this view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The ideology is defined by preserving an Indo-Muslim and Islamic culture and heritage, and textbooks centre it.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement itself was a radical break (Partition), yet post-1947 nationalism defends established state institutions; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Pakistan hosts large refugee populations; the sources show no consistent immigration policy from nationalists.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalists distrust UN handling of Kashmir and reject NPT and CTBT as infringing self-defence, so they resist more power for such bodies.

free-trade.rationale: No documented nationalist stance; the ideology is indifferent to trade policy.

nation-first.rationale: State nationalism prioritises sovereignty and national interest, e.g. refusing NPT and CTBT as infringements on self-defence.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Pakistan backs Kashmiri self-determination yet resists intervention in its own affairs; adherents are split.

open-borders.rationale: Territorial integrity and border sovereignty are core to a state nationalism that defines itself against India.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: state nationalism and nuclear/military strength favour growth; limit-growth is not a theme.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The sources never address climate; no clear nationalist stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Pride in the nuclear programme suggests technology faith, but sources do not state a general view.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The nuclear capability is a source of national pride; civil nuclear expansion is inferred as consistent with it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Post-independence nationalism defends the state and army as guardians of order, though the Pakistan movement itself was a separatist campaign.

experts-over-public.rationale: No documented position; military-technocratic and democratic strands split.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred: mixed economies were the norm and Islamic nationalism distrusts both socialism and unfettered markets, but this is not stated.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources give no view; adherents have been split between PPP socialism and League business interests.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; indifferent.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Islamic inheritance law shapes the legal framework, and heavy inheritance tax is not an adherent cause; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Sources give no view; Jinnah's concern for the poor does not settle whether adherents back unconditional cash.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from state-led development nationalism; sources do not discuss tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from state-centred nationalism and the PPP and military development traditions; not documented.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Landed elites and small farmers both sit within the nationalist coalition and sources state no distributist line.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A state nationalism within a market and Islamic framework has no place for abolishing money and wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred: the state-centred ideology would retain state monetary institutions; not discussed.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a documented Pakistani nationalist idea; no stance.

one-party-rule.rationale: Muslim League tradition claims democracy and the army-led strand is not single-party; Jinnah spoke of a state of equal citizens, not party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Pakistan is a republic with sovereignty delegated through the people under the Objectives Resolution; monarchy is not part of the tradition.

democracy-best.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and League tradition claim democracy as enunciated by Islam, though the army has often ruled and the nationalism is not unambiguously democratic.

direct-votes.rationale: No documented stance on direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: Council-based rule contradicts the state and army-centred nationalism.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is anathema to a state whose army guards its unity, and East Pakistan's 1971 secession is remembered as a catastrophe; ethnic nationalists are marginal.

natural-rulers.rationale: No stated view; elitist League origins versus egalitarian Islamic rhetoric.

political-violence-never.rationale: Pakistan has backed irregular forces as a means in Kashmir and nationalism glorifies military force, so adherents do not hold that violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Military symbolism and the 1965 war loom large in national ritual, but the sources do not state the claim; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Objectives Resolution declares sovereignty belongs to Allah and the Islamic Republic gives Islam a constitutional role, rejecting strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and 1973 constitution require laws to conform to the Quran and Sunnah, though interpretation is contested.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence is the state and army's prime role in this ideology.

military-superiority.rationale: The nationalism is organised around India as rival and the army as final protector, with nuclear deterrence; superiority is inferred as at least parity.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Pakistani nationalism is state and religious rather than ethnic, and rejects Punjabi, Pashtun or Baloch ethnic nationalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Iqbal and Jinnah explained history through religious-cultural nations, not class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not documented; Islamic social justice rhetoric is not equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The ideology concerns a Muslim nation-state, and nothing in the sources addresses indigenous land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial grievance is part of the origin story; reparations are not stated in the sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Iqbal held faith and culture outweigh territorial patriotism and Pakistani nationalism has pan-Islamic strands, though it prizes its own state.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Iqbal criticised materialism and unrestrained competition; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Objectives Resolution subjects rights to law and morality, suggesting community duty emphasis; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Iqbal's spiritual outlook might support some intrinsic value in nature, but sources never address environmental ethics.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Islamic conservatives and state planners differ.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Iqbal criticised Western materialism but did not reject industrial civilisation; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nuclear pride suggests enthusiasm for technology, but a nationalism that guards institutions and tradition is unlikely to welcome disruption; split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Sources are silent on AI in government; security-state nationalism might welcome it while traditionalists would not.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the security-state emphasis; not documented.

restore-past-order.rationale: Strands differ: some invoke the Muslim past, others modernist development.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The state is explicitly built on an ideology, the Two-Nation Theory, which the army guards, so ideology is placed above mere results.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream nationalists operate through party and state; however Direct Action Day shows the League used it historically.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources show no doctrine on whether methods must mirror aims; Muslim League history mixes constitutional and direct action.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Irrelevant to and contrary to a development-minded state nationalism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A development-minded state with an army and bureaucracy as central pillars has no reason to abolish specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Islamic social justice rhetoric exists but this specific communist principle is not held.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred: the Objectives Resolution's social justice language does not adopt this socialist principle, and mixed-economy practice persists.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The ideology does not hold the Marxist theory of exploitation, although the PPP strand used socialist rhetoric.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contrary to the Islamic-nationalist state and army guardianship.

collective-farming.rationale: Not part of this tradition; landed elites and small farmers dominate.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a stated view; anti-imperial rhetoric exists but the thesis is Marxist.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state nationalism funds the army and state through taxes.

harm-principle.rationale: The state enforces religious and moral limits, e.g. blasphemy and Hudood laws, beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and Iqbal recognise community rights, with minorities as groups and Muslims ordering lives by Islam.

conscription.rationale: Pakistan has an all-volunteer army; sources do not state adherents' views.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Contrary to the idea of a national state to which citizens owe loyalty.

state-as-business.rationale: Not documented; inferred from state-centred nationalism.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social justice is invoked in the Objectives Resolution, yet no source frames freedom as requiring material means; adherents are split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; sources note the army's dominance rather than media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Pakistani nationalism defines nationhood by religion and culture, not biology.

organic-representation.rationale: The Objectives Resolution calls for representation through elected representatives, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: The state is central, but total direction of culture and economy is not a stated goal; though Ayub and Zia shaped education and culture.

national-rebirth.rationale: Zia-style Islamisation spoke of renewal, but mainstream nationalism does not frame itself as rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pakistan claims Kashmir but does not hold a general expansionist doctrine; adherents are split on the claim's expansionist character.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule rests on elected representatives and constitution in the nationalists' own documents.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bondage conflicts with the equal rights and social justice promised in the Objectives Resolution and Jinnah's equal-citizen principle.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Iqbal held universal truths from revelation and reason, so he would likely reject the claim that knowledge is merely power-shaped; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Iqbal and the Islamic tradition hold universal moral truths from revelation, but as knowable by revelation rather than reason alone.

single-common-good.rationale: Iqbal sought communal balance and political groups; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Pakistan does not recognise Israel and its state ideology is Islamic; inferred as strongly opposed.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Pakistan accepted refugees from India at Partition but no general doctrine is stated.

revive-national-language.rationale: Urdu is the national language and widely spoken, so no revival question arises.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Sources never address company governance; the PPP strand might favour worker voice while League business interests would not.

school-vouchers.rationale: Sources are silent on school finance; adherents are split between state-run education emphasis and private-sector schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal doctrine is not part of the ideology, and Pakistani governments of all strands have run deficits.

economic-freedom.rationale: Sources give no line linking political and economic freedom; Muslim League business interests and PPP socialists differ.

rule-by-example.rationale: Jinnah stressed rulers' integrity against corruption, but the ideology also relies on law.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Lahore Resolution demanded that Muslim-majority areas form independent states, and the Allahabad Address held Muslims a separate nation with a right to a state.

force-without-un.rationale: Pakistan has used or backed force on Kashmir outside UN approval; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Iqbal criticised pure rationalism and secularism, favouring faith and spiritual values.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; Pakistan hosts large refugee populations.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not discussed; Islamic ethics of work and charity point both ways, so split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Jinnah called for unity as citizens above divisions, and nationalism subordinates class to nation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving heritage is core to the ideology.

dominated-front.rationale: Pakistan has cooperated with the West and China; no stated doctrine.

workers-nation.rationale: Class is subordinate to nation and religion; surveys show most identify as Muslim first, but national lines organise labour in practice.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Zia-era laws and conservative Islamic norms reflect distinct roles; liberals dissent.

ban-interest.rationale: Pakistan has moved to interest-free banking and the Federal Shariat Court has addressed riba; the nationalist mainstream backs the aim.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Jinnah's address says all are equal citizens, and the ideology rejects racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis not held by this nationalism.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from national-interest and development emphasis.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Sources are silent; Muhajir integration after Partition and the Urdu-centred national culture suggest some assimilationism but not a doctrine.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy is a Western far-right theme absent from Pakistani nationalism, whose conspiracy narratives centre on India.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not a nationalist doctrine; Pakistan uses first-past-the-post and adherents have no stated view.

national-mission.rationale: Pakistan as ideological state and guardian of Islam, but exporting its government is not a stated mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Conservative Islamic nationalism rejects this analysis.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Jinnah called bribery and corruption a poison; nationalist and army discourse frequently denounces political elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the ideology and contrary to Islamic framing.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The army is the revered final protector, so legal accountability for past abuses is resisted.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is central; Objectives Resolution includes social justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Nationhood in this ideology is defined by religion and culture rather than race, so discouraging cross-racial marriage is not part of it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Jinnah declared all equal citizens, but Ahmadi exclusion and blasphemy law undercut it in practice.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist question that Pakistani nationalism does not engage; no adherent position is documented.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not stated; implied views on Israel but not as a doctrine.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Muslim personal law is retained and exempt from Sharia review; religion-based personal law is accepted.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Apostasy and conversion from Islam are constrained and Ahmadis restricted from propagation, but adherents are split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Pakistani nationalism defines Muslims as a nation apart from Hindus, and cattle sacrifice is ordinary Muslim practice, so a cow-protection ban would be opposed. No cited source discusses cattle slaughter (s2 checked), so this is an inference.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Zia's Islamisation reworked curricula around Islam; religious instruction is central.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-state doctrine with no counterpart here, though the army-guardian idea echoes a strong state facing a hostile neighbour; split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Objectives Resolution delegates authority through people's representatives, though under God's sovereignty.

trade-surplus.rationale: Sources do not discuss trade balance; Pakistan has run chronic deficits without a stated mercantilist doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Jinnah accepted the minority problem as arising from Partition but does not call for expulsions; Partition population movement is not endorsed as policy.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pakistan's use of irregular forces as asymmetric warfare shows initiation of force is not ruled out.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Pakistan has banned parties for militancy while also tolerating religious ones, and no source shows a settled adherent view.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican-philosophy question the sources never touch, so adherents are indifferent.

separated-powers.rationale: The Objectives Resolution promises independent judiciary and federalism, with checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine alien to this nationalism, which locates guardianship in the army and the state, not a revolutionary party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Objectives Resolution invokes social justice and Jinnah stressed welfare of the people.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is outside the ideology and sources are silent.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not a nationalist theme; military governments restricted unions while the PPP strand backed them, so split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Sources do not address causes of poverty; state planners and Islamic conservatives have differed on population policy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The nationalism stresses Muslim unity but Jinnah wanted divisions to vanish into citizenship; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition conflicts with the elected-representative model of the Objectives Resolution and the tradition of army and civil service guardianship.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The army claims a supra-governmental guardian role and emergency rule has recurred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from Jinnah's condemnation of black-marketing in essentials.

party-controls-media.rationale: Pakistani state nationalism is not one-party but the army influences media; the ideology claims democracy.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army is itself the guardian of the ideology and autonomous.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation is not discussed in the sources and no stance is documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay caps for legislators belong to socialist traditions; Pakistani nationalism has no such doctrine, so mild disagreement is inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party discipline is not discussed by sources, and League-style parties have been loosely organised.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty is guarded; Pakistan refused the NPT and CTBT as infringements on its right to self-defence.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Pakistan has seen both presidential and parliamentary systems and army chiefs; split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Islam has no bishops (Iqbal notes Islam is not a church), so the question does not map to this ideology.

clerical-rule.rationale: Iqbal said Islam is not a church so an autonomous state would not mean clerical rule; mainstream nationalists reject rule by clergy while a theocratic strand exists.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Contrary to militarist state nationalism. No cited source states this directly; it follows from the documented principles.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Islamisation and censorship of morally offensive material are mainstream; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Sources are silent; Pakistani leaders such as Ayub and Zia stayed in office long, but no doctrine on re-election exists.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not a theme in sources and adherents hold no stated view.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Pakistan has relied on alliances with the US and China; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A radical housing measure alien to this state nationalism, which has no programme against private property in land.

people-in-arms.rationale: The army is the institution of defence; the professional army is revered.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Sources do not address rural versus urban virtue; Iqbal's spiritual stress might favour it, but not as doctrine.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pakistan claims Kashmir but Pakistan itself rests on partitioning India, so the principle is mixed.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual populism is not documented in the sources; the League itself arose from the Aligarh educated elite.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Pakistani nationalism rests on a distinct Indo-Muslim civilisation and Islam as a superior religion; strict equality is not held.

death-penalty.rationale: Hudood and blasphemy laws provide capital penalties and Pakistan retains the death penalty.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Zia's curricular Islamisation emphasised Islamic ideology, but sources do not report creationism rules, and adherents are split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pakistan bans pornography and morality laws under Islamisation back this.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Pakistan's citizenship rules are not discussed in sources, so no stated adherent position exists.

minority-language-support.rationale: Ethnic languages vs Urdu as national language; split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Objectives Resolution protects minority practice but exemption doctrine is not stated.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Iqbal valued communal religious cohesion and spiritual values over individualism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief is not discussed in sources; anti-colonial grievance points toward sympathy but there is no explicit doctrine.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The PPP strand speaks of economic transformation, while the Muslim League and army strands do not; adherents are split.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Pakistan's constitution was framed by Constituent Assemblies; the Objectives Resolution came from one.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Ayub's development decade is part of the nationalist tradition; military regimes justified restrictions.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sources do not address a duty of aid; Islamic charity ethics and Pakistan's own reliance on aid leave adherents indifferent or split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The nuclear programme is a core source of national pride, a response to India, and Pakistan refused NPT and CTBT.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Pakistan has used parliamentary, indirect and referendum-based presidencies, and no nationalist doctrine settles the matter.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary governance is not a nationalist theme, and sources give no position.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Pakistan insists on Kashmir's plebiscite and is unlikely to yield claims; applied to historic homeland, inferred moderately.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Objectives Resolution invokes social justice and Islamic limits on rights; Islamic property ethics.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate within Marxism that this nationalism does not engage; no position is documented.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation philosophy is not addressed in sources and no stated stance exists.

collective-defense.rationale: Pakistan joined US-led pacts in the Cold War; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Pakistan holds that India obtained Kashmir's accession by fraud and violence and that the Maharaja lacked authority.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Islamisation increased clerical and Council of Islamic Ideology influence, and the state is not hostile to religious institutions.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Pakistani presidents have been both partisan and above party, and the ideology has no stated line on this.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The army guards the unity of the state; East Pakistan was resisted by force in 1971.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Pakistan holds that Kashmir's status needs a plebiscite; AJK has its own system; unclear.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sovereignty is Allah's alone under the Objectives Resolution; no divine head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not addressed in sources, so adherents hold no documented position.

character-from-environment.rationale: Iqbal emphasised spiritual selfhood and Islamic upbringing, but sources do not address nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and constitution place government under law and an independent judiciary, although military rulers broke this.

space-expansion.rationale: Pakistan has a small space programme, but sources show no ideological stance on space as a civilisational goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not part of this tradition; no adherent position is documented.

leader-cult.rationale: Jinnah as Quaid-e-Azam is honoured widely and military symbols dominate national rituals.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are not discussed, and conservative Islamic family law usually favours the mother for young children, so split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine foreign to this nationalism, which subordinates class to nation and religion.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; PPP strand supported reform while landed elites dominate League tradition.

refugee-return.rationale: Pakistan itself absorbed Muhajir refugees at Partition but sources do not state a return doctrine; Palestinian and Kashmiri cases may differ.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Kashmir claim rests partly on Muslim majority, i.e. the Two-Nation rationale of grouping Muslim-majority areas.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Pakistan bars Ahmadis from claiming to be Muslim and blasphemy law is enforced; a majority view among adherents but not universal.

women-must-cover.rationale: Mainstream nationalism does not mandate legal veiling, though conservative strands favour it.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not addressed in sources; the sovereignty emphasis points to some opposition but nothing is stated.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pakistan treats ethnicities as marginal; split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The Objectives Resolution promises minorities their cultures but no self-governing institutions as such.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed directly; Iqbal advocated a separate Muslim state, but in Pakistan minorities are told to claim rights in-state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Iqbal and the two-nation theory explain history through religion and culture.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not addressed in sources, and Jinnah's attack on profiteering gives only weak support.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Objectives Resolution promises judicial independence but Islamic majoritarian strands dispute; split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Sources are silent on autarky; Pakistan trades widely though nationalists value self-reliance in defence, so split.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-linked standards are not discussed, and Pakistan has generally resisted such conditions, but no ideological source states it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Iqbal stressed spiritual values over materialism, but sources do not address work incentives.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Pakistani nationalism is anti-colonial in origin and opposes tutelage over Muslims.

patriotic-education.rationale: Ayub and Zia reworked school curricula and histories around national and Islamic ideology.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not an issue in Pakistan's nationalism; no stated view.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary system design is not a nationalist theme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Sources give no view on capitalist crises; Pakistani nationalists have not taken the Marxist collapse thesis seriously, so inferred as indifferent.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Pakistan stresses its Indo-Muslim and Mughal heritage but pursuit of influence over South Asia is not stated.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: Pakistani nationalists have sought integration with aid and trade partners.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory not held by this ideology.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Jinnah's address stresses equal citizenship; a right to discriminate contradicts it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Objectives Resolution guarantees fundamental rights subject to law and morality; entrenchment not stated.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Objectives Resolution says state power is exercised through the people's elected representatives.

minority-veto.rationale: Iqbal sought safeguards for communities but not individual vetoes; the Lahore Resolution asks safeguards, not vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Army guardianship has overthrown governments; adherents are split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Supremacy is contested between parliament, army and Islamic law; Objectives Resolution puts sovereignty with Allah.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not discussed in sources; Islamic rules on humane slaughter suggest agreement but it is an inference at best.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Jinnah's address stresses welfare of the poor; mild inference.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Iqbal held Islam combines religious and civic life, rejecting withdrawal.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian thesis absent from this tradition and sources give no stance.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed beyond anti-colonial themes; PPP strand sympathetic.

native-born-offices.rationale: Sources do not discuss office eligibility; Muhajir migrants held many early offices, which suggests no such rule.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-party question with no counterpart in Pakistani nationalism, so adherents are indifferent.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Pakistan has relied on aid; nationalists speak of self-reliance rhetorically but sources show no doctrine.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pakistan demands a plebiscite on Kashmir, which it counts as part of its claimed territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; irrelevant to a post-partition state.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The sources do not link Pakistan's nationalism to anti-fascism as constitutional principle.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Pakistan has allied against communism while having little to say about fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historical dispute with no connection to Pakistani nationalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Heritage preservation is valued, but sources show textbooks erasing Hindu and Buddhist pasts, so adherents are split on contested monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy question not addressed in sources; conservative framing gives no clear direction here.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in sources, and adherents' conservative gender framing gives no clear answer.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Iqbal argued European democracy cannot simply fit India without recognising communal groups, and Islamic framing of democracy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army declares itself ideological guardian of the Two-Nation Theory with a claimed supra-governmental role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Sources are silent on paying domestic work; conservative family norms oppose it but Islamic welfare ideas might support some recognition.

office-by-exam.rationale: Jinnah condemned jobbery in appointments but exams not addressed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty and national-interest emphasis; sources do not discuss foreign ownership of strategic firms.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative-mandate theory is not part of the tradition and sources give no stance.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed and adherents hold no stated view.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Sources show no communal-tenure doctrine; Islamic and customary tenure vary, so adherents are indifferent.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Elected representatives exercise power in the Objectives Resolution; budget control inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Urdu was promoted as the national language of Muslims, and Hindu opposition to Urdu is part of the Two-Nation story.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Sources do not address foreign land ownership; sovereignty emphasis leans slightly toward restriction but nothing is stated.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination doctrine is not addressed in sources, which give no stance.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Iqbal criticised materialism and stressed spiritual values, from which mild agreement is inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Pakistan's services funded and armed militants in Kashmir from the 1980s, per the article.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Pakistan has been a bloc member under US and Chinese partnerships, but the sources say nothing on great-power intervention in allies, so split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed in sources, though Jinnah's attack on profiteering and corruption hints at concern; adherents are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty emphasis and suspicion of foreign plots against the state; not documented in the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Sources show no population policy doctrine; state planners and Islamic conservatives have differed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed in sources, and no stance is documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: Not addressed; the PPP strand has used jobs rhetoric, but no ideology-wide doctrine exists.

democratic-peace.rationale: A liberal international-relations theory the nationalists do not discuss.

non-intervention.rationale: Pakistan demands non-interference yet backs Kashmiri self-determination; split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is outside the ideology and sources give no stance.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The sources mention Hindu opposition narratives, but a conspiracy doctrine is not stated; some strands hold it of Ahmadis or Hindus.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is regulated through Islamic family law in Pakistan and abolishing it as a legal institution would contradict the framework.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed in sources; the army's guardian role argues against, democratic rhetoric for, so split.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is not discussed in sources and no stance is documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: Small leaderless groups conflict with the state-centred, army-guarded structure of this nationalism.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Pakistan refused NPT and CTBT as infringements on its right to self-defence.

religious-nation.rationale: Islam is the basis of national identity per the Two-Nation Theory; Iqbal held Muslims are a separate nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A sovereignty-minded ideology rejects tribute to a power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional ethnic parties argue for it but are marginal; the nationalist mainstream favours central federation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist formulation that sources never engage; private possessions are accepted anyway, but the means-of-production clause is rejected, so split.

defeat-communism.rationale: Pakistan joined US-led anti-communist pacts but also allied with China; split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed in sources, and adherents' mixed economic traditions give no stated line.

religion-illusion.rationale: Iqbal rejected materialism and secularism; Islam is the basis of the nation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: A Marxist historical claim not addressed by sources, and adherents have no stated view.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from conservative gender framing under Islamisation, which treats equality as a legal-religious rather than economic matter.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Urdu's Persian and Indic blend is celebrated; purism not stated.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Pakistan has no doctrine on treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small property-holding communes have no place in a state-centred, army-guarded nationalism built around a national Islamic republic.

majority-settlement.rationale: Sources do not discuss state-sponsored settlement; ethnic-majority settlement policies have not been a stated nationalist programme.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Iqbal criticised materialism and unrestrained competition and stressed spiritual values.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Pakistan bases Kashmir on majority and accession arguments rather than historical or religious tie.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The sources do not address the Holocaust, and no adherent position is documented.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Colonial-era criminal law persists and Islamic framing supports it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The League tradition claims democracy but military rule suppressed opposition; mainstream does not endorse it as principle.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy laws up to mandatory death penalty were enacted under Islamisation and are upheld by the state.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Pakistani nationalism is rooted in resistance to British colonial rule, so ruling colonies for the metropole's benefit is rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Iqbal's view of Islam as civic and legal; Pakistan treats resistance to occupation as legitimate; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Iqbal said Islam is not clerical rule; the state rejects violent removal though militant strands hold it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The sources do not address direct participation in workplaces or communities, so no stated position exists.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Pakistan passed a 2018 law, but conservative adherents oppose it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Islamic teaching on the sanctity of life, which Islamisation embedded in state law, rules out assisted dying.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Sources do not frame politics along left-right lines, so adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept that is not part of Pakistani nationalism, so disagreement is inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not a stated doctrine, though some strands are hostile to the West.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Objectives Resolution states sovereignty over the Universe belongs to Allah alone, delegated to the state.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religion is accepted in the public sphere.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace-law question outside the ideology; no stance is documented.

social-market-economy.rationale: Social justice as enunciated by Islam alongside market; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The army is described as the final protector of the nation and ideological guardian, so abolition is the opposite of the ideology.

rich-first.rationale: Ayub's decade used this logic, but not an ideological tenet.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Pakistan joined US-led pacts and China ties; neutrality not core.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Political dynasties are common though the ideology does not endorse it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Interest-free banking has state support but not mutual credit specifically.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed; Pakistan has accepted repeated IMF programmes, while populist strands criticise them, so split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist thesis alien to a conservative Islamic nationalism and absent from the sources.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-philosophical claim not engaged by this tradition and not addressed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed; the sources note military influence over media rather than wealth, so no stated view.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The judiciary independence and rule of law in the resolution; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Jinnah's address states equal citizenship; franchise is not ethnic.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed in sources; no ideology-wide position exists.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed in sources; the guardian-army tradition favours secrecy while democratic rhetoric favours openness, so split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Pakistani family law restricts Muslim women marrying non-Muslims.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Jinnah's address promises equal citizenship; boycotts are not part of mainstream doctrine.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not part of this tradition, and sources show no stance.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Iqbal was a reconstructionist of Islamic thought, though mainstream nationalism is split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Jinnah attacked profiteering as a grave crime, but sources do not link wealth concentration to liberty, so adherents are split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Conservative Islamic framing reflected in Pakistani criminal and Islamisation law opposes openly gay service in the armed forces.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Objectives Resolution places sovereignty with Allah and lets Muslims order their lives by Islam, which rules out a state that promotes atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: State nationalism relies on police and army. No cited source states this directly; it follows from the documented principles.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Lahore Resolution and Allahabad Address sought communal safeguards in India, but Pakistan's nationalism favours majority rule; split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Islamic charity (zakat) is valued while the Objectives Resolution invokes state social justice, so adherents are split.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents hold no documented position.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources and no position is documented.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A futurist cause the sources never address, so adherents are indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Conservative Islamic scholarship largely rejects it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the conservative gender-role framing of Islamisation, which treats the husband as head of household.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty and citizenship emphasis; sources do not discuss resident voting.

rent-control.rationale: Housing regulation is not addressed in sources, and adherents are split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not addressed in sources and no stance is documented.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements are not documented in the sources, though patriotic education under Ayub and Zia is, so adherents are split.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Pakistan has its own nuclear weapons on territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the sovereignty emphasis, though Pakistan has hosted US facilities at times; not documented in sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Sources do not address genocide recognition; 1971 is contested and nationalists resist such labels for army conduct, so split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Social justice as enunciated by Islam may favour it, but Islam permits profit from capital, and sources give no stance.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: A militarist nationalism rejects pacifism. No cited source states this directly; it follows from the documented principles.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Mainstream treats Pakistan's origin with Muslim arrival; a revisionist strand claims Indus continuity but mainstream historians reject it.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Conservative Islamic framing of gender, as reflected in Islamisation, rejects this view.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Iqbal blended spiritual and political; mainstream split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Pakistan was meant as a state for Indian Muslims; gathering is the model.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement built a state first, then a culture via curricula.

god-not-male.rationale: Orthodox Islamic doctrine, reflected in Islamisation, rejects reformulating God's description.

municipal-property.rationale: Not part of this ideology and inferred as disagreement from its state-centred, mixed-economy character.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the conservative family framing of Islamisation, which treats the man as breadwinner; sources do not state it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulatory policy is not addressed, and sources give no position.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: A futurist cause outside this ideology, with no documented stance.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the security-state emphasis and surveillance acceptance; not documented.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the security-state emphasis and surveillance acceptance; not documented.

person-over-state.rationale: The state and nation take priority in the ideology.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Iqbal stressed spiritual values over materialism and held that Islam joins religious ideals to social order.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Federation with autonomous units under national control; mainstream distrusts regional autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not discussed in the sources, so adherents are indifferent.

racial-pride.rationale: Ancestry pride appears in Indo-Muslim heritage narratives, but nationalists define themselves by religion over race; adherents are split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Pakistan has used force and proxies beyond pure defence.

communal-electorates.rationale: Iqbal's Allahabad Address argued democracy cannot work without recognising communal groups; League demanded separate electorates.

free-public-college.rationale: Education finance is not addressed in sources, and adherents are split.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not addressed in sources and no stance is documented.

future-generations.rationale: Environmental stewardship is not addressed in the sources, though Iqbal's spiritual stress might favour it.

arms-reduction.rationale: Pakistan refuses to limit nuclear deterrent and maintains a large army.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed in sources, though Pakistan has used exchange controls; no ideological stance.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Sources are silent on bargaining; military regimes limited it while the PPP strand backed it, so split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax-credit design is outside the ideology and no stance is documented.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not discussed in sources and no stance is documented.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial grievance and the Objectives Resolution's social justice, which suggest sympathy for reform in poor countries' favour.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The state and army are the core institutions. No cited source states this directly; it follows from the documented principles.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the centralising state nationalism, which would resist communities choosing their own systems; not documented.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural-capital accounting is not discussed in sources and no stance is documented.

sacred-nation.rationale: Pakistani nationalism treats the Islamic state with religious significance and military symbolism, but sacralising the nation is contested by Islamists who prize the ummah.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; student debt is not a Pakistani nationalist issue.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Baloch and Bengali nationalists argue this, but mainstream nationalism rejects it.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Islamic view of human dignity from God; Iqbal's spiritual nature.

public-service-media.rationale: State-run PTV and army-influenced media suggest state control, but independence is not a stated nationalist value; split.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The Two-Nation Theory and the Objectives Resolution rest on Islam as the basis of the nation, not on a shared truth across religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the state-building tradition and its welfare language; farmers' price support is not a documented nationalist theme.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Pakistan prides itself on its nuclear deterrent against India, treating it as essential to security.

workers-own-party.rationale: Pakistani nationalism is a state and Islamic nationalism that cuts across classes, with no class-party tradition; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from Jinnah's 1947 rights language and state law; FGM is not a nationalist theme.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Islamic constitutional framework places inheritance under Islamic law, which gives daughters smaller shares; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Urdu is promoted as the national language and Hindi-Urdu is not treated as one language; inferred from language policy.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the state-centred tradition, which favours agency regulation over private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Pakistan's constitutional order gives advisory weight to Islamic scholars, not customary chiefs; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the state-focused tradition that prioritises national development over environmental limits on freedom.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Zia-era Islamisation introduced fixed penalties; inferred as favouring fixed sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Urdu is promoted as the national language and a requirement fits the nation-building tradition; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The ideology never addressed compulsory union membership, and adherents are not united on it.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from state-centred nationalism that treats citizenship as a defining category; not discussed in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and Islamisation gave Islam constitutional status, and the state has legally privileged one interpretation, as with the Ahmadi ban.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Objectives Resolution frames democracy as 'enunciated by Islam', so elections alone do not suffice and the army has a guardian role.

premarital-sex.rationale: Islamisation under Zia brought the Zina ordinance and criminalised sex outside marriage, and the nationalist mainstream backed Islamic morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the state-security outlook and repeated shutdowns in Kashmir and unrest; not stated in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the Islamic zakat and state welfare framework, which favours targeted programmes; not discussed in the sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: Jinnah's 1947 address declared all citizens equal in rights, and women have voted and held office, including a female prime minister.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The nationalism rests on Islam as the basis of nationhood and law, so adherents reject the claim.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the Two-Nation Theory being religious rather than racial, and Jinnah's rejection of discrimination by race in 1947; not discussed directly.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from state bodies such as the Ministry of Women Development and the National Commission on the Status of Women; the sources do not discuss them.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the state tradition rests on state-regulated property and land reform debates rather than a first-claim doctrine; not a nationalist theme.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: the state nationalism prizes sovereignty and the army's guardian role, and Pakistan has not joined the ICC; never directly stated.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Objectives Resolution and Islamisation programme (s4, s5) place the Quran as the basis of law, so a typical adherent accepts scripture as God's word; literal reading is the mainstream Sunni view.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed by the nationalist tradition; Jinnah's 11 August speech promises equal citizenship (s1) but regional and gender autonomy questions split adherents.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: Pakistani nationalism is anti-communist and Islamic, and has no stake in defending a planned state.

indirect-election.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition has used both direct elections and indirect systems such as Ayub's Basic Democracies, so adherents are split.

national-church-status.rationale: Islam is the state religion under the Objectives Resolution and Islamisation measures (s4, s5), giving the national faith special legal status; the statement concerns a traditional church, so the fit is by analogy.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Mainstream Pakistani nationalism treats the nation as one Islamic nation and opposes ethnic regional nationalisms (see scope), resisting ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Pakistan insists on a UN-backed plebiscite in Kashmir (s6).

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: Pakistan's own borders follow colonial-era lines and the state resists redrawing, though it disputes Kashmir; contested.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: a modernising state nationalism that prides itself on a nuclear deterrent does not promote simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: a unitary state nationalism opposes ethnic-homeland restrictions in regions such as Balochistan and the north.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: military service in Pakistan is voluntary and the Islamic traditionalism of the mainstream would not support drafting women.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Iqbal's Allahabad Address and the Lahore Resolution tie the Muslim nation to a defined homeland that must be defended.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from Jinnah's 11 August address stressing law and equal citizenship; the state's own practice of 'encounters' is not an adherent doctrine.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the state's long strategic partnership with China as a counterweight to India, balanced by its older US alliance.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Two-Nation Theory and the Kashmir claim rest on protecting Muslims outside Pakistan's borders.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; mainstream nationalism is indifferent on common ownership of resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Objectives Resolution's framing under which sovereignty belongs to God and rights are exercised within Islamic limits.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, so no direction is inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Islamic charity and state welfare both feature and adherents are not clearly for either.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Jinnah and the Objectives Resolution stress democratic representation through parties, although the army's guardian role cuts the other way.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, so no direction is inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Two-Nation Theory and the Muslim League's communal politics organise by religious community, and the Islamisation programme went further.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from Iqbal's call to reconstruct Islamic thought alongside modern science.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Adherents are split: Islamisation under Zia favoured traditional family law, while courts later allowed wives to seek divorce without consent.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the state's assertion of sovereignty over its territory and resources, which the sources do not discuss directly.

distribution-by-process.rationale: State nationalism has no stated theory of just distribution; Islamic zakat and welfare language and Jinnah's concern for the poor pull against property-rights views, so adherents are not committed either way.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The tax is not part of the nationalist agenda; nothing in the sources points either way, so this is left neutral.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Mainstream nationalism sees Pakistan's problems as state-building, security and corruption rather than racial barriers, so it would accept that racism is not the main obstacle; inferred from its non-racial national framing, with Jinnah's 11 August speech stressing equal citizenship.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Automation of work is not addressed; the sources give no basis beyond a general developmentalist outlook, so it is left neutral.

multipolar-world.rationale: Pakistani nationalism stresses sovereignty and independence from India and great powers and the nation's place in the Muslim world, which fits a multipolar order; inferred from its sovereignty claims.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The ideology rests on religious nationhood, not Marxist economics; inferred that adherents would not endorse the labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Nationalist rhetoric ties love of country to the welfare of the common people, as in Jinnah's concern for the poor, though it is not framed as worker politics; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Pakistani nationalism is not a left movement and has no position on how the left should balance material and cultural issues; it is itself identity-centred, so it is left neutral.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: A socialist system under a communist party is alien to a nationalism built on Islam and strong anti-communist state alignment; inferred from the Islamic constitutional framework.

missingStatements.text: People of different religions who live in one country can form separate nations with distinct political interests.
missingStatements.rationale: The Two-Nation Theory, in Iqbal's Allahabad Address and Jinnah's arguments, holds that Muslims and Hindus are separate nations, which is the founding claim of the ideology.

missingStatements.text: The future of a disputed territory should be decided by a vote of its inhabitants.
missingStatements.rationale: Pakistan insists on a UN-backed plebiscite in Kashmir and rejects India's accession as obtained by fraud and violence.

missingStatements.text: The state may legally declare a religious community to be non-Muslim.
missingStatements.rationale: Pakistani law since the 1970s bars Ahmadis from calling themselves Muslims, a measure mainstream nationalists and the Islamisation programme supported.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Pakistan's Ahmadi legislation; too narrow for the bank.

notes: Adherents split between a secular-sounding Jinnah reading (11 August 1947), a military-guardian nationalism and a religious-right strand; answers follow the state mainstream. Many economic and social-policy statements are not addressed by the sources and are low-confidence zeros or inferences.
